entries.title: GitHub Actions step uses a mutable tag or branch reference. Tags and branch names can be silently repointed by the action owner, enabling supply-chain attacks — as seen in the trivy-action and kics-github-action compromises. Pin the reference to a full 40-character commit SHA instead, e.g. `uses: actions/checkout@8ade135a41bc03ea155e62e844d188df1ea18608`.
entries.reason: Accepted: ci/github-actions.yml is a copy-paste TEMPLATE, not a live workflow. It uses readable version tags (@v4) so the snippet is legible to someone reading the docs, and its header instructs the reader to pin to commit SHAs before relying on it. This repository's own live workflow, .github/workflows/vibecheck.yml, is fully SHA-pinned and carries none of these findings. Scope note: this entry covers ALL occurrences of this rule in this file (5 when accepted), because the scanner emits an identical message for each. Re-review if the template stops being documentation-only.
